mount-greylock-scenic-byway.title: Mount Greylock Scenic Byway
mount-greylock-scenic-byway.slogan: Up the highest ground in Massachusetts from one side and down the other.

waypoints.name: Lanesborough
waypoints.advice: Lanesborough is where the day begins. Next is Rockwell Road, climbing 450 m.

waypoints.name: Rockwell Road
waypoints.advice: Rockwell Road comes up 7 km in. The road climbs 450 m over at least 8 km before it, hard. Reckon on about 4 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is Greylock summit, climbing 263 m.

waypoints.name: Greylock summit
waypoints.advice: 1063 m, and the road stops climbing. The road climbs 263 m on the way up to it, steadily. Reckon on about 6 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Nothing on this route is higher. Next is Notch Road, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: Notch Road
waypoints.advice: Notch Road, late in the day at 700 m. You lose 363 m on the way down to it, hard. Reckon on about 3 °C colder than the valley, and more in the wind. Next is North Adams, mostly downhill.

waypoints.name: North Adams
waypoints.advice: Back at North Adams. That is the ride. You lose 490 m on the way down to it, steeply.

scenicChapters.title: Mohawk Trail
scenicChapters.narrative: For 5 km this is Mohawk Trail, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it — expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Mohawk Trail
scenicChapters.narrative: 490 m come off over 6 km at around 8.1%. The road gives back what the climb took, faster than it took it. Brakes early, eyes far ahead. A descent this long asks more of concentration than of pace.

mount-greylock-scenic-byway.story: From Lanesborough it runs 26 km to North Adams; allow about 30 min of riding. It goes by way of Rockwell Road and Notch Road. Greylock summit is the high point. It tops out at 1,063 m. It was put together for the scenery rather than the shortest line.
